pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: 1918 flu -> 'post-influenza depression.' Great Depression -> massive suicide increase. 2008 -> spike in depression, substance abuse. COVID -> youth mental health crisis.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Delayed psychological processing + economic stress + isolation effects compound over time
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Mental health crisis always peaks 1-2 years after the economic/health crisis. Systems never prepared for this second wave.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: Youth mental health crisis 2022-2024: anxiety, depression, loneliness at record levels post-COVID.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: Youth depression doubled from 2019-2023. Suicide is now #2 cause of death for ages 10-14. Therapist waitlists: 3-6 months.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Every crisis has a physical phase and a mental phase. We only prepare for the first.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Natural disasters hit the same vulnerable areas repeatedly
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: New Orleans: flooded in 1927, 1965, 2005 (Katrina). Japan: tsunamis every 50-100 years in same regions. Bangladesh: floods repeatedly in same deltas. Rebuild in same spot every time.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Attachment to place + short memory + 'it won't happen again' + economic inertia
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Katrina: $125B damage. 1,836 deaths. Rebuilt in same flood zones. New flood in future: guaranteed.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: Climate change making this worse. Building in wildfire zones (California), flood plains (Houston), hurricane paths (Florida).
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: US natural disaster costs: $92.9B (2023). 70% of Americans live in areas with increased disaster risk. Insurance industry retreating from high-risk areas.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Building in disaster-prone areas with government-subsidized insurance is paying people to make the same mistake repeatedly.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Cyberattacks follow the same escalation as physical warfare
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: Stuxnet (2010): first cyber weapon. WannaCry (2017): hospitals held ransom. SolarWinds (2020): supply chain attack on US government. Colonial Pipeline (2021): fuel shortage from ransomware.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Digital infrastructure dependency + inadequate security investment + nation-state espionage incentives
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Escalating frequency and severity. But investment in cybersecurity still lags the threat.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: AI-powered cyberattacks next frontier. AI can generate malware, find vulnerabilities, social engineer at scale.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: Ransomware payments: $1.1B (2023, record). Average downtime from attack: 24 days. 83% of organizations experienced multiple breaches.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Digital infrastructure is the new critical infrastructure. We protect it like it's optional.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Energy crises repeat when dependence on single source isn't diversified
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: 1973: OPEC embargo, gas lines. 1979: Iranian revolution, prices doubled. 2022: Russia-Ukraine, European gas crisis. Same pattern: dependence -> disruption -> panic -> partial diversification -> new dependence.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Cheapest source wins over resilient source + political capture + short memory
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Each crisis: 'never again dependent on X.' Then dependence shifts to new source. Europe: Russia gas -> LNG + renewables.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: Rare earth dependence on China (70% of processing). EV battery material concentration.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: China processes 70% of lithium, 90% of rare earths. European gas from Russia dropped from 40% to 15% post-2022.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Energy diversification is expensive until the crisis that makes concentration catastrophic.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Public health systems defunded between crises
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: After every pandemic: funding increase. Between pandemics: gradual defunding. US CDC budget in real terms lower in 2019 than 2010. WHO perpetually underfunded.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Invisible successes get no credit + budget pressure on prevention vs treatment
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Each pandemic finds systems weaker than they should be. COVID: US had pandemic playbook, defunded the team to execute it.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: Post-COVID pandemic preparedness already declining. Political will evaporating.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: 75% of WHO pandemic preparedness recommendations from 2019 were unfunded when COVID hit. US public health workforce declined 15% from 2008-2019.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Prevention is invisible when it works. That invisibility leads to defunding.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: War and conflict follow economic crises with predictable lag
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: Great Depression -> rise of fascism -> WWII (10-year lag). 2008 financial crisis -> populism surge -> Brexit, Trump, global authoritarian wave (8-year lag). Economic pain creates political extremism.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Economic desperation -> scapegoating -> strongman appeal -> conflict
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Pattern is predictive: major economic crisis predicts political instability 5-10 years later.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: COVID economic damage + inflation -> populism surge globally. Taiwan, Ukraine, Middle East tensions.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: Democracy Index: declined every year since 2015. Authoritarian-leaning countries: 72% of world population.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Economic crises are not just financial events. They are the seeds of the next political crisis.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Food system fragility revealed by every major disruption
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: Irish Famine 1845: monoculture failure (potato). Dust Bowl 1930s: soil destruction from overfarming. COVID: empty shelves despite full warehouses (distribution failure). 2022: Ukraine war disrupted 25% of global wheat.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Efficiency over resilience + monoculture risk + long supply chains
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Each crisis: temporary local food interest. Then return to global supply chains. Vulnerability unchanged.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: 3 companies control 90% of grain trade. 4 countries produce 87% of corn exports.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: 30% of food is wasted globally while 735M go hungry. 3 countries: 87% of corn exports.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Food system efficiency and food system resilience are opposite goals. We always choose efficiency.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Technology adoption accelerates during crises then partially reverses
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: WWI: radio adoption accelerated. WWII: computing, jet engines, nuclear. COVID: remote work, telemedicine, e-commerce, digital payments all jumped 5-10 years forward in 6 months.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Necessity as mother of adoption + inertia overcome by urgency + partial reversion after crisis
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Each crisis: technology adoption jumps forward. Some reverts, but never to pre-crisis levels. Ratchet effect.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: Remote work: peaked at 60% (2020), settled at 28% (2024). Higher than pre-COVID 5%. Permanent shift.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: Remote work: 5% (2019) -> 60% (2020) -> 28% (2024). Telemedicine visits: 1% -> 46% -> 15%. Ratchet effect confirmed.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: Crises don't create technology trends. They accelerate trends that were already inevitable.

pandemic_and_crisis_response.pattern: Insurance industry retreats from risk areas after disasters, leaving populations exposed
pandemic_and_crisis_response.what_happened: After Hurricane Andrew (1992): 9 insurers left Florida. After 2020-2023 disasters: State Farm left California. Nationwide pulling back from climate-exposed areas.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.human_nature_at_play: Market pricing reality vs political desire for affordable coverage + adverse selection
pandemic_and_crisis_response.outcome: Government becomes insurer of last resort. Taxpayers subsidize building in dangerous areas. Cycle continues.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_parallel: Climate change making insurance unaffordable in Florida, California, Louisiana. Federal flood insurance: $20B in debt.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.modern_data: Florida homeowner insurance: $4,231/year (3x national average). 7 insurers left Florida since 2022. NFIP: $20.5B in debt.
pandemic_and_crisis_response.lesson_ignored: When insurance companies leave, they're telling you the risk is real. Ignoring this message is expensive.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Entertainment used to distract population from declining living standards
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Roman government provided free grain and gladiatorial games. At peak, 1/3 of Roman population received free food. Colosseum held 50,000. Citizens gave up political participation for entertainment.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Comfort over freedom + spectacle as social control + apathy through satisfaction
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Politically disengaged citizenry. When barbarians came, citizens didn't fight. Empire fell partly from internal apathy.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Social media as modern circus. TikTok, Netflix, gaming. Bread: stimulus checks, SNAP, UBI debates.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Average American: 7.5 hours screen time/day. Netflix users: 238M. US government assistance: 59M recipients.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: A population entertained into apathy will not defend its own interests.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: New form of credit creates illusion of wealth that precedes collapse
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Installment buying invented for sewing machines, then pianos, then everything. First department store credit. Middle class could 'live like' upper class. Debt normalized for the first time.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Status consumption + debt normalization + keeping up appearances
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Consumer debt became permanent feature of economy. Set pattern for 20th century credit expansion.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: BNPL making debt invisible. 'Pay in 4' makes everything seem affordable. Average Gen Z has debt at 22.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: US consumer debt: $17.5T (2024, record). Average household: $104,215 in total debt.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Making debt invisible doesn't make it disappear. It makes it grow.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Credit expansion creates unsustainable consumption followed by painful contraction
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Consumer credit doubled in the 1920s. 60% of cars bought on installment. 'Buy now, pay later' for everything from radios to refrigerators. Debt-fueled consumption created illusion of permanent prosperity.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Instant gratification + debt normalization + confusing access with ownership
consumption_and_debt.outcome: When crash came, consumers couldn't pay. Deflation made debts heavier. Depression lasted 10 years.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: 2020s consumer credit at all-time highs. Credit card debt $1.13T. Auto loans $1.6T. Student loans $1.7T.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Total US consumer debt: $17.5T. Debt-to-income ratio: highest since 2008.
consumption_and_debt.data_source: Federal Reserve, NY Fed Consumer Credit Panel
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Debt-fueled prosperity is borrowed from the future. The future always collects.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Credit card industry designs systems to maximize debt, not convenience
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Diners Club (1950) -> BankAmericard (1958) -> universal credit. Industry revenue model: 80% from interest, not merchant fees. Minimum payments designed to maximize interest paid.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Present bias + minimum payment illusion + compound interest against the consumer
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Average $7,951 credit card debt per household. $130B+ in interest paid annually. Designed to keep people in debt.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: BNPL companies using identical psychology with digital interface. Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: $1.13T US credit card debt (2024, record). Average APR: 24.6%. Minimum payment on $5,000: takes 22 years to pay off.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: The credit industry's business model requires your perpetual indebtedness.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Subprime lending extends credit to those who can't afford it
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Subprime mortgages: $625B issued in 2005. NINJA loans. Adjustable rates resetting from 2% to 12%. Banks earned origination fees regardless of borrower default.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Predatory lending + American Dream exploitation + misaligned incentives (originate-to-distribute)
consumption_and_debt.outcome: 10M foreclosures. $10T in home equity destroyed. Banks bailed out. Homeowners not.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Subprime auto loans growing. BNPL extending credit to those who can't afford traditional credit.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Subprime auto loans: $260B outstanding. Delinquency rates: 7.7% (highest since 2010). BNPL late payments: 42%.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Extending credit to people who can't afford repayment helps the lender, not the borrower.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: BNPL is the new subprime -- different package, same debt
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: BNPL usage grew 400% since 2020. Klarna, Afterpay, Affirm. Users average 4.7 BNPL loans simultaneously. Not reported to credit bureaus (initially). Targeted at Gen Z.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Pain of paying removed + small payments feel manageable + debt invisibility
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Delinquencies rising. Regulators catching up. Credit bureaus starting to include BNPL in reports.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: This IS the current cycle. Same as credit cards (1960s), subprime mortgages (2000s). New packaging, same debt.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: 42% of BNPL users missed a payment. Average user: 4.7 concurrent BNPL loans. 25% used BNPL for groceries.
consumption_and_debt.data_source: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, LendingTree
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Making debt feel painless doesn't make it painless. It makes it invisible until it isn't.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Student loan debt follows the same trajectory as housing debt
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: College costs rose 1,200% since 1980 (vs 236% inflation). Student debt: $1.77T. Average graduate: $37,718 in debt. Unlike all other debt, cannot be discharged in bankruptcy.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Credential inflation + 'investment in yourself' narrative + government-guaranteed lending removing market discipline
consumption_and_debt.outcome: 45M Americans carry student debt. 21% in default or delinquent. Average repayment time: 20 years.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Same dynamic in coding bootcamps ($15K-$30K) and AI certifications. ISAs and income-share as new model.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: $1.77T student debt. Average payment: $503/month. 43% of borrowers not making progress on principal.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Government-guaranteed loans remove market discipline from pricing. Costs always rise to absorb available credit.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Hedonic treadmill: income rises, spending rises faster
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Consistent finding: happiness increases with income only up to ~$75K-$100K. Beyond that, lifestyle inflation absorbs gains. 25% of people earning $100K+ live paycheck to paycheck.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Hedonic adaptation + social comparison + moving goalpost + status signaling
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Every income bracket has people who 'can't make ends meet.' Problem is spending, not earning.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Social media amplifying lifestyle inflation. Seeing everyone's highlight reel. Consumption as identity.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: 25% of those earning $100K+ live paycheck to paycheck. 35% of $200K+ earners have less than $5K savings.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Wealth is not what you earn. It's what you don't spend.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: National debt grows until crisis forces austerity
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Greece defaulted 5 times since independence (1826). Argentina 9 times. US debt: $34T (123% of GDP). Every government borrows more in good times and bad times.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Political incentive to spend + no incentive to save + future generations bear the cost
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Pattern: borrow -> grow -> borrow more -> crisis -> austerity -> repeat. Japan: 263% debt-to-GDP and still adding.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: US adding $1T in debt every 100 days (2024). Interest payments: $1T/year (more than defense).
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: US national debt: $34T. Interest alone: $1T/year. Debt-to-GDP: 123%. Adding $1T every 100 days.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: No government in history has voluntarily reduced debt during peacetime. The constraint is always a crisis.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Subscription model extracts more over time while feeling cheaper
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Everything became subscription: software, entertainment, fitness, food, clothing, cars. Average American: 12 subscriptions, $219/month. Companies prefer subscriptions: predictable revenue, higher LTV.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Small recurring payments feel affordable + cancellation friction + subscription amnesia
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Americans spend $2,628/year on subscriptions. 42% forget at least one active subscription. Companies count on inertia.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: AI tools all subscription. Adobe, Microsoft, Netflix all raised prices 20-40% since going subscription-only.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Average American: 12 subscriptions, $219/month ($2,628/year). 42% have at least one forgotten subscription.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Subscriptions feel like small rivers. Together they're an ocean draining your account.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Luxury goods marketed to middle class create aspirational debt
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Luxury brands: shifted from old money to 'accessible luxury.' Coach, Michael Kors, Louis Vuitton entry-level. Middle class spending on luxury at 3x income growth rate.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Status signaling + social media comparison + identity through consumption
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Personal luxury goods market: $390B. But customer base shifted from wealthy to aspirational debtors.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Social media accelerating aspirational spending. 18-29 year olds most likely to finance luxury purchases.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Gen Z luxury spending growing 3x faster than other generations. 45% finance luxury purchases. Average luxury debt: $2,400.
consumption_and_debt.data_source: Bain Luxury Study, Afterpay consumer report
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: If you're financing a luxury purchase, you can't afford it. The brand knows this and profits from it.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Auto loan terms keep extending to maintain 'affordable' payments on unaffordable cars
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Average new car price: $48,759 (2024). Average auto loan: $35,445 over 69 months. Negative equity: 25% of trade-ins. Loan terms extending to 84 months to keep payments low.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Monthly payment focus (not total cost) + car as identity + keeping up with neighbors
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Americans owe $1.6T in auto debt. Delinquencies rising. Repos increasing. Underwater borrowers trapped.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Same pattern as housing: extend terms, hide total cost, create underwater borrowers.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: $1.6T auto debt. 17.3% of new loans are 73-84 months. 25% of trade-ins have negative equity averaging $6,255.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: A longer loan doesn't make a car more affordable. It makes the debt more expensive.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Medical debt uniquely American pattern of healthcare as consumption
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: US healthcare spending: $4.5T/year (17.3% of GDP). 100M Americans carry medical debt. #1 cause of bankruptcy. No other developed country has this problem.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Fear of death exploited + opaque pricing + insurance complexity + political failure
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Medical debt: $220B in collections. Average bankruptcy medical debt: $10,000. Life expectancy declining despite highest spending.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic): $1,349/month in US, $59 in Germany. Same drug, 23x markup.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: 100M Americans have medical debt. US life expectancy: 77.5 (below Cuba, Costa Rica). Healthcare spend: 2x any other country.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: A system where illness creates poverty is not a healthcare system. It's an extraction system.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Gambling repackaged as entertainment/investment in each generation
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Horse racing -> slot machines -> state lotteries (1964+) -> casinos -> online poker (2003) -> sports betting (2018 legalization) -> crypto trading -> prediction markets.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Dopamine seeking + 'skill' illusion + social normalization + accessible platforms
consumption_and_debt.outcome: US gambling revenue: $66.5B (2023, record). Sports betting: $10.2B. Problem gambling rising with accessibility.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Prediction markets (Polymarket). Meme coin trading. 0DTE options. All gambling with different names.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Sports betting grew 44.5% in 2023. Problem gambling: 2.6M adults (severe). 9.5M at risk.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Each generation repackages gambling and calls it something else. The psychology is identical.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Savings rates collapse when access to credit is easy
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: US savings rate: 17% (1975) -> 7.5% (2000) -> 2.2% (2005, pre-crisis) -> brief spike to 32% (COVID stimulus) -> 3.7% (2024). Inverse correlation with credit availability.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Present bias + credit substituting for savings + cultural shift from thrift to consumption
consumption_and_debt.outcome: 56% of Americans can't cover $1,000 emergency. Entirely dependent on continued access to credit.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Gen Z savings rate lower than any previous generation at same age. But also earning less in real terms.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: 56% can't cover $1,000 emergency. Personal savings rate: 3.7%. Retirement savings gap: $3.68T.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: A society that doesn't save is one crisis away from collapse.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Paycheck to paycheck existence across all income levels
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Not just low-income: 68% of all Americans live paycheck to paycheck. 25% of $100K+ earners too. Lifestyle inflation + debt + no emergency fund = universal fragility.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Consumption expansion to match income + social comparison + present bias + financial illiteracy
consumption_and_debt.outcome: One job loss, one medical bill, one car repair from crisis for most Americans. Economic 'growth' is fragile.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Same pattern globally. UK: 59% paycheck to paycheck. Australia: 50%. Not uniquely American.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: 68% of Americans paycheck to paycheck (2024). Including 25% earning $100K+. Median savings: $8,000.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Financial security is not about income level. It's about the gap between income and spending.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Housing affordability crisis follows same pattern in every major city
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Home price-to-income ratio: 3x (1970s) -> 5x (2000) -> 7x nationally, 12x in coastal cities (2024). Each generation further from homeownership than the last.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Housing as investment (not shelter) + NIMBY blocking supply + speculation + low interest rate legacy
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Homeownership rate for under-35: 39% (vs 56% in 1960). Generation locked out of primary wealth-building mechanism.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Global phenomenon: London, Sydney, Toronto, Hong Kong, Bandung (Indonesia), all have similar ratios.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Median US home: $412K. Median household income: $75K. Ratio: 5.5x. San Francisco: 12x. Mortgage payment: 42% of median income.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: When housing becomes an investment class, it stops being affordable shelter. These are contradictory goals.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Fast fashion creates consumption addiction with environmental destruction
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Zara (1990s) revolutionized fashion: 12 collections/year became 52. Shein: 6,000 new items per DAY. Average garment worn 7 times. 92M tons of textile waste annually.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Novelty seeking + social media pressure + disposability normalization + low prices hiding true costs
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Fashion industry: 10% of global emissions. More clothes produced than can be consumed. 85% ends in landfills.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Shein: $30B revenue. Ultra-fast fashion accelerating. 'Haul' culture on TikTok.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Shein: 6,000 new items/day. Average American buys 68 garments/year. 85% of textiles go to landfill.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Cheap prices externalize costs to the environment and exploited workers.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Food delivery apps increase spending while decreasing cooking skills
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: DoorDash, UberEats, Grubhub. Average delivery order: $35 (vs $10 cooking at home). Monthly delivery spend: $350+ for regular users. Tips, fees, and markups add 40-60% to restaurant prices.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Convenience addiction + time-money tradeoff distortion + cooking skill atrophy
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Average American spends 55% of food budget on eating out/delivery (up from 25% in 1970).
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: AI-ordered groceries and meals next step. Further removing the connection between food cost and consumption.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Food delivery market: $350B globally. Average markup vs cooking: 300%. Regular users spend $4,000+/year on delivery fees alone.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Convenience has a compound cost. $10/day in delivery fees = $3,650/year = $36,500/decade.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Wealth effect from asset prices creates spending from unrealized gains
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: When stocks or homes rise, people spend more -- even without selling. 'Paper wealth' drives real spending. When assets fall, spending collapses disproportionately.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Mental accounting + unrealized gains feel real + lifestyle calibrated to portfolio peak
consumption_and_debt.outcome: 2000: wealth effect reversed, recession. 2008: reversed, crisis. 2022: reversed, spending cut.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: Crypto wealth effect: people spent based on unrealized crypto gains in 2021. Then everything reversed.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Every $1 increase in stock wealth generates $0.03-$0.05 in spending. Every $1 increase in housing wealth: $0.05-$0.09.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Unrealized gains are not income. Spending them is spending money you don't have.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Technology amplifies consumption speed without increasing consumption satisfaction
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: Smartphone + apps made buying instant. Amazon 1-click. Apple Pay face scan. Micro-transactions in games. Impulse buying: decision to purchase now takes 2 seconds, not 2 days.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Friction reduction removes deliberation + impulse purchasing amplified + regret comes after
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Average return rate: 16.5% (up from 8% pre-mobile). Impulse purchase regret: 88% of buyers.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: AI personal shoppers removing even the browsing friction. Anticipatory shipping. Buy before you decide.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: 88% of impulse buyers feel regret. Average impulse spend: $314/month. Returns: $816B in merchandise (2022).
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Making buying easier doesn't make buying smarter. It makes buying more impulsive and wasteful.

consumption_and_debt.pattern: Children targeted as consumers from increasingly young ages
consumption_and_debt.what_happened: 1950s: Saturday morning cartoons as ads. 1990s: internet advertising to kids. 2010s: YouTube Kids exploitation. 2020s: in-app purchases, Roblox economy, Fortnite skins. Kids spending parents' money digitally.
consumption_and_debt.human_nature_at_play: Children's vulnerability to marketing + parental guilt spending + digital payment removing friction
consumption_and_debt.outcome: Children influence $1.2T in spending. Kids' in-app purchases: $4.2B (2023). FTC struggles to regulate.
consumption_and_debt.modern_parallel: AI chatbots marketed to children. Concern about AI manipulation of young users. Character.ai controversy.
consumption_and_debt.modern_data: Children influence $1.2T in annual spending. Kids' screen time: 7+ hours/day. Loot box spending by minors: $380M/year.
consumption_and_debt.lesson_ignored: Every generation targets children as consumers more aggressively than the last.
